Claim: `domain:ui` PM seat (`os-tesla`) — dispatching an `os-dev` seat now, R16.

Branch: `claude/issue-8978-alert-dialog-destructive-confirm`

Clause-②: yes

Reason for the `yes`, recorded at dispatch and ⛔ not revisable on delivery: every route this card leaves open touches a published face — a new authorable key on the `alert-dialog` renderer schema, or a changed default on `AlertDialogAction`, or both. 「拿不准 ⇒ 按 yes」.

## Why this dispatches on zero comments

The heuristic "zero comments ⇒ untriaged" has an exception, and this card is it: the body was written by a **director seat** splitting this out **by maintainer ruling** on 2026-09-10, and it carries decision batch #70's verbatim 「同意」 for the capability itself. That is stronger than a triage comment, not weaker. ⇒ read who wrote the body.

{
  "issue": 8978,
  "status": "done",

  "premise_still_valid": true,
  "summary": "Wired the destructive confirm as a NEW authorable key `AlertDialogSchema.actionVariant?: 'default' | 'destructive'`, read by the `alert-dialog` renderer onto the confirm button, with a DOM pin, docs, two catalog fixtures restored and a changeset. HEAD 4a617ceb8 on base fe9e0d054.

SHAPE CHOSEN, AND THE ARGUMENT AGAINST R2'S TOMBSTONE. Spelling is `actionVariant`, NOT `confirmVariant`. (1) The retired key stays retired: a document authoring `confirmVariant` still reds, same `invalid_type` code, so no published spelling goes from refusing an author to accepting one. That is the whole content of the maintainer's 2026-09-10 remark. (2) `actionVariant` is not a new dialect: this node already calls that button `action` three times (`actionText`, `onAction`, `AlertDialogAction`), and the SAME retirement pointed `confirmLabel` at `actionText`. Reviving `confirm*` for the variant while `confirm*` for the label is tombstoned would publish two prefixes for one button. (3) One published string did move: the tombstone MESSAGE, from 'NO surviving spelling ... a separate question that needs its own card' to naming `actionVariant`. This card IS that card, so the sentence was stale on arrival; the key's verdict is unchanged. Two existing pins were re-derived onto the other side of that question rather than deleted.

VALUE DOMAIN: two, not `ButtonSchema.variant`'s six, BY MEASUREMENT (see M5). Declaring a value the node cannot render would be the `confirmVariant` disease one level down, at the value instead of the key.

M1 - `buttonVariants` (printed from packages/components/src/ui/button.tsx, not assumed): six variants default|destructive|outline|secondary|ghost|link plus a size axis, defaultVariants variant:'default' size:'default'. `destructive` emits `bg-destructive text-destructive-foreground hover:bg-destructive/90`; the default the confirm button is pinned to emits `bg-primary text-primary-foreground hover:bg-primary/90`. YES, destructive is among them. Also measured: `buttonVariants()` is byte-identical to `buttonVariants({variant: undefined})`. The pin never types those class names in - it computes the token sets FROM `buttonVariants` at run time, with an ORACLE control that reds if the two variants ever stop differing.

M2 - BLAST RADIUS: zero, because the default is NOT changed. Call sites enumerated by `git grep AlertDialogAction`: apps/console ApprovalsInboxPage (4), app-shell InvitationsPage / MembersPage / SettingsPage (2) / ActionConfirmDialog, components NotificationAlerts (2), plugin-detail RelatedList, plugin-form DrawerForm + ModalForm, plugin-gantt ObjectGantt, and the SDUI renderer. Every one passes no variant; the renderer passes className=undefined for an unauthored key and `cn(buttonVariants(), undefined)` is byte-identical to `cn(buttonVariants())`. Asserted as the pin's UNTOUCHED control, which compares two whole rendered dialogs, not as an argument.

M2 SIDE-FINDING THAT CHANGED THE ROUTE: the card's suggested edit to packages/components/src/ui/alert-dialog.tsx is FORBIDDEN - AGENTS.md Commandment #7 makes packages/components/src/ui/** a No-Touch zone regenerated by `pnpm shadcn:update`, and `alert-dialog` is a tracked component (`pnpm shadcn:list`). The sanctioned escape hatch is a declared patch in scripts/shadcn-local-patches.mjs, whose own header says to keep the payload OUT of src/ui/. So the variant is applied as a className OVERRIDE from the renderer - not invented: packages/components/src/notifications/NotificationAlerts.tsx already expresses a footer variant on this very button the same way, with a comment saying why.

M3 - THE CATALOG SITES: found, and the count is TWO, not three. Commit ed5fee9be (PR #7962) converted FOUR fixtures under examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/components-overlay-alert-dialog/ off a phantom `actions` array and its own message says 'the per-button variant is DROPPED'. Dropped CONFIRM-button variants: basic-alert-dialog 'Continue' = destructive; confirmation-dialog 'Save' = default; custom-actions 'Yes, Continue' = default; destructive-action 'Delete' = destructive. I am not rounding two up to three. The reading that yields exactly three is a different denominator - the dropped variants the primitives could not reproduce for free: two destructive confirms plus the `ghost` CANCEL in confirmation-dialog (the two outline cancels and two default confirms are what the primitives already emit). That is a plausible reconstruction of the ruling's sentence, NOT a fact I measured it against. The two destructive confirms are restored in this PR.

M4 - ANCHORS RE-MEASURED BY TEXT (card read 2c208d5bb; this branch bases on fe9e0d054). All still exactly as described: the `buttonVariants` import from './button'; the confirm button's `className={cn(buttonVariants(), className)}` with NO argument; the cancel button's `buttonVariants({ variant: "outline" })`; and the renderer's one-line `{schema.actionText && ...AlertDialogAction onClick={schema.onAction}...}`. Premise holds; only the line numbers moved. Every zero-hit reading in this run carried a lit control in the same command - e.g. the source-text pin sweep's control hit packages/i18n/src/__tests__/residue-namespaces-3546.test.tsx:161 for KanbanImpl.tsx, exactly as the dispatch specified, and the sweep widened to my changed-file names and to scripts/ found nothing outside the pins I own or updated.

M5 - DOES A KEY NEED ADDING: YES, and the sweep is what says so. The repo HAS an idiom - a key spelled `variant` at `buttonVariants`' domain on the node that OWNS the button: 18 renderer registrations declare a `variant` input and about 20 renderers read `schema.variant`; `ButtonSchema.variant` (packages/types/src/form.ts) is the exact six-member union, read at renderers/form/button.tsx. BUT no existing idiom reaches THIS button: `AlertDialogSchema` declares no variant key, there is no footer slot, the footer is generated from two STRINGS, and the `content` slot renders above the footer and is not an `AlertDialogAction`. The M3 fixtures prove it from the author's side - they reached for `type:'button'` nodes with `variant` (the idiom) and the renderer carried none of it. So the idiom governs the SPELLING and VALUE DOMAIN, not whether a key is needed.

M5 SECOND HALF - WHY TWO VALUES, measured through the real renderer, not inherited from the idiom: an override can only displace a baked-in class that shares its tailwind-merge group. default = clean; destructive = clean; secondary = clean (but nothing asked for it, and widening later is non-breaking while narrowing is not); outline LEAKS `text-primary-foreground`; ghost LEAKS `bg-primary text-primary-foreground`; link LEAKS `bg-primary hover:bg-primary/90`. The pin's MECHANISM- legs render each of the three lossy values THROUGH the renderer and assert the leftovers are still on the node, so that table is re-derived on every run rather than recorded - widening the union without widening the mechanism reds.",

On-disk proof both runs: HEAD blob hash printed; anchor `grep -c` 1 BEFORE and 0 AFTER; post-mutation `git hash-object` differs from the HEAD blob; restore via `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH` from an `EXIT INT TERM` trap; restoration proven by an EMPTY `git diff HEAD` (printed 'diff-empty=YES'), never by an exit code. No build/dist step is involved - vitest aliases the @object-ui packages to src (vitest.config.mts resolve.alias), so there is no stale-dist channel here.
  RUN 1 = 4 failed | 13 passed. RUN 2 (after the repair) = 7 failed | 10 passed. WIRED = 17 passed.
  leg-by-leg (wired / ablated-run2): WIRED,ORACLE,INSTRUMENT,UNTOUCHED controls PASS/PASS; LEG 1 destructive tokens present PASS/FAIL; LEG 1b displaced tokens gone PASS/FAIL; LEG 2 default path unchanged PASS/PASS; LEG 3 cancel untouched + confirm moved PASS/FAIL; MECHANISM+ default PASS/PASS; MECHANISM+ destructive PASS/FAIL; MECHANISM- outline|ghost|link PASS/FAIL times 3; authoring-face closure (4 legs) PASS/PASS.
  THE FINDING, flagged per the dispatch's star: in RUN 1 the three MECHANISM- legs stayed GREEN while the thing they name was deleted, because each asserted only that the primitive's baked-in classes were STILL on the node - trivially true of a renderer that applies nothing. Fixed, not noted: each now asserts ARRIVAL first (the tokens the variant itself emits ARE on the node) and only then the loss. Commit 4a617ceb8.

  type-check: pnpm --filter @object-ui/types --filter @object-ui/components run type-check -> 'Done' on both, VERDICT command-exit 0. Both include tsconfig.test.json, which is what compiles the @ts-expect-error and Equal legs. It caught a real narrow-parameter error in my pin on the first attempt.

This IS the whole population `turbo run lint` covers for the two packages this diff touches, so it is not a narrowing of the file set. Type-aware linting is NOT enabled - the flat config extends tseslint.configs.recommended and languageOptions carries only ecmaVersion and globals, with zero hits for `projectService` against a lit control of 1 hit for `languageOptions` - so this diff cannot move a verdict on any file it does not contain.

GATES GREEN (exit 0, reading each gate's own printed verdict line, never a bare dollar-question): changeset:check, check:changeset-claims, check-changeset-presence, check:doc-types, check:doc-fences, check:doc-example-ids, check:new-line-citations (0 new citations), check:handler-key-reads, check:control-bytes, check:side-effects-array, check:unreferenced-sources, check:spec-symbols, check:element-data-source-declaration, check:prompt-keys, check:vi-mock-specifiers. Plus a manual control-byte self-scan over the changed files.

NOT MEASURED - three gates, one reason, all declared to CI, NONE recorded as green: check:sdui-registration-pins, check:doc-snippets and check:doc-examples all exit 2 = PREREQUISITE NOT MET. The first prints 'No console build to weigh at apps/console/dist/assets. This is exit 2, not a pass'. I attempted `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console build`: it needs every workspace package's dist (TS2307 'Cannot find module @object-ui/components' and friends), i.e. a whole-tree build, which is past this container's roughly 10 minute foreground cap. The cheap sibling of the first, check:side-effects-array, IS green, and this diff adds no module and no registration - only an `inputs` entry on a registration that already existed. pnpm shadcn:check also not run: weekly scheduled, needs the network, and this diff deliberately touches no file under packages/components/src/ui/.

TOOLCHAIN NOTE: my first dependency-closure build failed because I put --concurrency=2 AFTER --filter and pnpm forwarded it to `tsup --concurrency=2`. Re-run as `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/components^...' build` -> all 7 deps Done.",

    "noted, not filed: the `ghost` CANCEL variant. confirmation-dialog.json authored variant:'ghost' on its cancel button before PR #7962 stripped it. AlertDialogCancel hard-codes outline and there is no cancelVariant key. This card is the destructive CONFIRM; a cancel variant is a different capability with no ruling behind it, and the same override channel would carry neither ghost nor link anyway (measured, M5). Handler: whoever widens the override mechanism, i.e. the same PR that would widen actionVariant past two values. Not filed as a defect because nothing is broken - the key simply is not declared, so an author writing it is refused by name.",

It is internal React props, not authorable metadata, so it is in no filing category (not category c). Cited because it is the precedent this renderer's approach follows. Handler: whoever widens the union.",
    "noted, not filed: the card's line citations into alert-dialog.tsx and renderers/overlay/alert-dialog.tsx have drifted, as the card itself warned. Nothing to fix - recorded only so M4's re-measurement is not read as a correction to the card. Handler: none.",

I did not loop."
